# Tooltip — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a tooltip to label an icon-only control, or to add one short line of context that is useful but not worth permanent space. It appears on hover and on keyboard focus, and it must be dismissible without precision pointing — if the content is only reachable by hovering, it is unreachable on touch. Never put an action inside a tooltip, and never put information there that is not available some other way. If the explanation is long enough to need paragraphs, it is a help panel, not a tooltip.

### Usage

**Do**

- Name icon-only controls on hover and focus.
- Keep text to a few words.

**Don't**

- Don't duplicate visible labels — tooltips name the unnamed.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Container | resting | comp.tooltip.container | inverse-surface, 4px, level2 |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| TooltipProvider | Shares open/close timing across a group of tooltips, so one does not fire while another is still fading. Wrap a group once. |
| TooltipRoot | Owns the open state for one tooltip. Accepts `open`/`onOpenChange` to control it. |
| TooltipTrigger | The control the tooltip describes. Hover and focus on it open the tooltip. |
| TooltipContent | The label itself. Portals to the end of the document and positions itself against the trigger. |

### Deviations from Material 3

**K11** — spec: M3's component elevation table tabulates only the RICH tooltip at level 2; it names no plain tooltip.

Kern: The (plain) tooltip popup rests at elevation level 2.

Why: review-m3 ruled the plain-tooltip level a kern choice sharing the rich row's height, not a transcription of M3 (K11); the citation is the registry, not the spec row.

### FAQ

**Tooltip or label?**

Visible labels win; tooltips cover icon-only and truncated cases.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a tooltip when a control needs one line of extra explanation: what an icon-only button does, what a setting means. The design decision worth understanding is how it treats the text. `label` is the TRIGGER's own accessible name and `hint` is the supplementary line — and the hint is carried as `accessibilityHint` whether or not the surface is showing. That is deliberate: on touch there is no hover, so a tooltip that only exists while open would hold information nobody can reach. The text is never trapped behind the trigger. `placement` is `top` or `bottom`, and Material 3's default is above.

### Usage

**Do**

- Name icon-only controls: `label` is the accessible name, `hint` the supplementary text — two separate strings, on purpose.
- Keep the hint to a few words; explanations with actions are the rich tooltip's job.
- Let focus drive it — `open`/`onOpenChange` exist for the cases focus cannot cover, not as the default.

**Don't**

- Don't duplicate visible labels — tooltips name the unnamed.
- Don't put crucial information only in a tooltip — it must exist some other way too.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plain surface | resting | theme.color.inverseSurface | inverseSurface, extra-small corners, level 2 (3dp) |
| Plain label | resting | theme.color.inverseOnSurface | inverseOnSurface label text |
| Rich surface | resting | theme.color.surfaceContainer | surfaceContainer with 12/8/16dp padding and real buttons |

### Deviations from Material 3

**K11** — spec: M3's component elevation table tabulates only the RICH tooltip at level 2; it names no plain tooltip.

Kern: The (plain) tooltip popup rests at elevation level 2.

Why: review-m3 ruled the plain-tooltip level a kern choice sharing the rich row's height, not a transcription of M3 (K11); the citation is the registry, not the spec row.

### FAQ

**Plain or rich?**

A label for an unnamed control means plain. A subhead plus supporting text plus actions means rich — and if the rich surface has no actions and no subhead, that is a plain tooltip.

**How does this differ from the web tooltip?**

Same trigger contract (focus opens) and same K11 level-2 resting elevation on the plain surface. The plain surface is inert (`pointerEvents="none"`, `role="text"`) so touches fall through to the trigger; the rich surface takes touches because its actions are interactive by spec.
